svg.text: BLUEPRINT 06: GREEN'S THEOREM & STOKES' CIRCULATION-CURL THEOREM ARCHITECTURE
Plane Circulation-Curl Bridge • Planar Area Engines • 3D Surface Invariance (Rubber Sheet) • GATE Stadium & Circle Drills

g.text: Converts a 2D closed line integral into an area double integral over enclosed region R:
oint_C ( M dx + N dy ) = iint_R ( dN/dx - dM/dy ) dx dy
Must be piecewise smooth, simple closed curve.
COUNTERCLOCKWISE (CCW); region R stays on the left.
If traversed Clockwise (CW), multiply integral by -1 !
PLANAR AREA COMPUTATION VIA LINE INTEGRALS
Choosing field coefficients such that (dN/dx - dM/dy) = 1 yields the enclosed area:
oint_C ( x dy - y dx ) = 2 x Area(R)
Whenever GATE asks for oint (x dy - y dx), immediately calculate 2 times the geometric area!
Evaluate oint_C (x dy - y dx) CCW along boundary of region formed by union of 2x3 rectangle and semicircle R=1:
oint_C (x dy - y dx) = 2 x Area(R)
Zero integration required! Completed in under 15 seconds vs 10 minutes of piecewise line integrals.
Relates circulation around boundary loop C to flux of curl through open surface S bounded by C:
oint_C F . dl = iint_S ( curl F ) . dS = iint_S ( grad x F ) . n_cap dS
Right-Hand Rule connects traverse of C with surface normal n_cap.
When S lies in x-y plane (n_cap = k): Stokes' Theorem REDUCES EXACTLY TO GREEN'S!
If S is closed, boundary C is empty (null loop) ==> oiint_S (grad x F) . dS == 0 !
iint_S1 (curl F).dS = iint_S2 (curl F).dS = iint_S3 (curl F).dS
The flux of curl is completely INDEPENDENT of the surface shape
as long as the boundary curve C remains identical!
GATE Strategy: Always replace curved surface S with the flat planar cap!
iint_S2 (curl F).dS - iint_S1 (curl F).dS = oiint_(S2 - S1) (curl F).dS = iiint_V [ div(curl F) ] dV = 0 [Q.E.D.]
Vector field F = y z i. Find oint_C F . dl along circle x^2 + y^2 = 1 in the plane z = 1 (CCW):
Step 1: Compute Curl of Vector Field F = (y z) i + 0 j + 0 k:
curl(F) = det [ i j k ; d/dx d/dy d/dz ; yz 0 0 ] = 0 i - (0 - y) j + (0 - z) k = y j - z k
Step 2: Choose Flat Planar Disk Surface S at z = 1:
Unit normal: n_cap = k ==> dS = dx dy k
Step 3: Evaluate Dot Product (curl F) . dS:
( y j - z k ) . ( k dx dy ) = -z dx dy
Since z = 1 everywhere on S: -z dx dy = -1 dx dy
W = iint_S (-1) dx dy = - Area(Circle) = - [ pi (1^2) ] = -pi [EXACT GATE MATCH]
int_A^B grad phi . dl = phi(B) - phi(A)
2D Plane strictly; C must be CCW!
S is OPEN surface bounded by C;
S must be a CLOSED surface!
STAGE 1: CHECK CURL OF VECTOR FIELD F FIRST!
- If YES and path is CLOSED => Answer = 0 IMMEDIATELY!
- If YES and path is OPEN => Answer = phi(B) - phi(A) (Find potential, bypass path!)
STAGE 2: IF curl(F) != 0 AND PATH IS 2D CLOSED LOOP:
Apply Green's Theorem: oint (M dx + N dy) = iint (dN/dx - dM/dy) dA
- If (dN/dx - dM/dy) is CONSTANT k => Answer = k x Area(R)!
Zero double integration needed; only elementary geometry (rectangles, circles)!
STAGE 3: IF curl(F) != 0 AND PATH IS 3D CLOSED LOOP:
Apply Stokes' Theorem: oint F . dl = iint_S (curl F) . dS
- Choose the FLATTEST, SIMPLEST planar surface capping loop C!
Example: For circle x^2+y^2=1 at z=1, use flat disk at z=1 (n_cap = k)!
THE 3 FATAL GATE PITFALLS TO AVOID:
1. Forgetting Path Orientation: CW line integral is NEGATIVE of CCW!
2. Stokes' on Closed Surface: Flux of curl through ANY closed surface is 0!
3. Singularity inside Green's region: (-y i + x j)/(x^2+y^2) does NOT satisfy
Green's theorem if (0, 0) is enclosed; yields 2pi, not 0!
Master Rule: Always inspect hypotheses before applying theorems!
